EventItemActionText:
TOWN OF VIENNA
Board of Zoning Appeals
Meeting Minutes
Wednesday, May 20, 2026

7:30 p.m.
Charles Robinson Jr. Town Hall – 127 Center Street South

The Board of Zoning Appeals met in regular session in the Vienna Town Hall, 127 Center Street South, Vienna, Virginia, on Wednesday, May 20, 2026, at 7:30 p.m.

Roll Call
Board Present: Mr. Brian Condon, Mr. Manpreet Dhanjal, Mrs. Mary McCullough, Mr. George Creed, Mr. Mike Gadell, and Mr. Michael Rettinger.
Mr. Robert Petersen was absent.

Staff present: 
Andrea West, Zoning Administrator; David Levy, Director of Planning and Zoning; Kelly O’Brien, Deputy Director of Planning and Zoning; Lyndsey Clouatre, Principal Planner; and Patricia Taylor, Board Clerk.

Request for approval of a Conditional Use Permit pursuant to Section 18-304 of the Town of Vienna Zoning and Subdivision Ordinance to relocate a portion of an existing art school (K-12 visual arts instruction) to 421 Church Street NE, Suite G, in the AE – Avenue East commercial zone.

Ms. Lyndsey Clouatre, Principal Planner, was sworn in and presented the staff report. She explained that the applicant proposed relocating a portion of an existing visual arts instruction business currently operating at 320 Maple Avenue East to 421 Church Street NE, Suite G. The school would provide fine arts instruction for K-12 students within the studio space. The previous use of the property was also used educational instruction. Ms. Clouatre reviewed the proposed hours of operation. Instruction will take place during afternoon and evening hours during the week (3:30 PM-7:30 PM Monday-Friday) and during morning and early afternoon hours on Saturdays (9:00 AM-2:00 PM). There would not be more than 10 students and two instructors at a given time. Staff found the application met the applicable Conditional Use Permit criteria and standards for specialized instruction uses.

The applicant, KJ Lee, of 320 Maple Avenue, Suite D, was sworn in and described the proposed operations and educational programming. Board members asked questions regarding the proposed use and operations. Mr. Gadell asked if the applicant could speak on the studio, the age range of students, and the instruction that will be taught. The applicant stated they teach mostly visual arts like drawing, painting, and arts and crafts. There will not be any work with fire, a kiln, or pottery. 

No public comments were offered.

Mr. Creed made a motion to close the public hearing. Mr. Dhanjal seconded the motion. The motion carried to close the public hearing.

Motion: 
Mr. Gadell moved to approve the Conditional Use Permit for specialized instruction pursuant to Section 18-304 of the Town Code at 421 Church Street NE, Suite G, in the AE – Avenue East commercial zone.

Second: Mr. Dhanjal

Vote: The motion carried. Yeas: 5,  Nays: 0, Abstentions: 1, with Mr. Condon abstaining.
EventItemTitle: 421 Church St NE Unit G - Request approval of a Conditional Use Permit for Specialized Instruction. The applicant intends to move a portion of their existing visual arts instruction business, currently located at 320 Maple Avenue East Suite E, to 421 Church Street NE Unit G.

EventItemActionText:
Request to amend an existing Conditional Use Permit to increase the number of students from 190 to 210 and staff from 42 to 50 in accordance with Section 18-304 for Green Hedges School, located at 415 Windover Avenue NW, in the RS-12.5 Residential Single-Unit zoning district. 

Ms. Kelly O’Brien, Deputy Director of Planning and Zoning, and Ms. Andrea West, Zoning Administrator, were sworn in and presented the staff report. Staff reviewed the proposed campus improvements, circulation changes, buffering enhancements, playground sound analysis, educational space supplements, and proposed phasing plan. Staff also summarized the Planning Commission recommendation and associated discussion topics.

Proposed site changes include construction of a new gymnasium, a relocated athletic field, new playgrounds, and a new academic building on Windover Avenue; demolition of the Rice Arts Center and several smaller accessory structures; and modernization and expansion of Kilmer Hall. Proposed traffic pattern modifications for Windover Avenue NW and Nutley Street NW for student pick-up and drop-off operations were also included.

The applicant team, Sara Mariska of Odin Feldman Pittleman, 1775 Wiehle Ave., Suite 400; Jessica Wadlow, Green Hedges School Board Chair, 415 Windover Ave NW; and Peter Barrett, Interim Head of School, 415 Windover Ave NW, were sworn in to speak. 

Peter Barrett, the Interim Head of School, spoke about the Green Hedges campus plan, summarizing the motivation behind the proposed improvements and the increases in student and staff numbers. 

The applicant's legal counsel, Sara Mariska of Odin Feldman Pittleman, discussed the school's approval history, the proposed campus modernization efforts, traffic circulation modifications, sound mitigation measures, and the school's long-term educational needs. A playground sound analysis, campus improvement plan, and educational space supplements were presented by the applicant. Ms. Mariska explained the proposed conditions included in the application. 

Jessica Wadlow, the Chair of the Green Hedges School Board, presented additional information about the proposed improvements and school operations, including drop-off and pick-up, and noise generated by the school's outdoor activities. 

Throughout the presentations, Board members asked questions regarding traffic circulation, noise impacts, buffering, playground operations, phasing, and long-term compliance with Conditional Use Permit conditions.

The Chair opened the floor for public comment. The following persons were sworn in and spoke on the agenda item: 

1.	Katherine Welch, 412 Knoll Street NW. 
Ms. Welch expressed concerns regarding increased traffic, playground noise, and compatibility of the proposed expansion with the surrounding residential neighborhood.
2.	Harry Proctor, 245 Nutley Street NW.
Mr. Proctor discussed concerns related to traffic circulation and the effectiveness of the proposed buffering and sound mitigation measures.
3.	Ingrid Lusis, 446 Windover Avenue NW.
Ms. Lucis expressed concerns regarding playground noise, construction impacts, and the campus’s long-term operational intensity.
4.	Aldis Lusis, 446 Windover Avenue NW.
Mr. Lucis discussed concerns regarding the enforcement of Conditional Use Permit conditions and the cumulative impacts of the proposed campus expansion.
5.	Ying Huang, 424 Knoll St NW.  
Mrs. Huang discussed concerns with the addition of lot coverage, traffic, and the safety of pedestrians, and the constrained area of the school. 
6.	Mike DiFrancisco, 434 Knoll Street NW.
Mr. DeFrancisco discussed concerns regarding traffic congestion, pedestrian safety, and neighborhood impacts associated with increased enrollment.
7.	Elizabeth DiFrancisco, 434 Knoll Street NW.
Ms. DeFrancisco expressed concerns regarding playground activity, traffic, and the scale of the proposed improvements relative to the surrounding neighborhood.
8.	Daryl Franklin, 331 Park Street NE.
Mr. Franklin expressed support for the school and the proposed modernization efforts.
9.	Penny Oszak, 221 Nutley Street NW.
Ms. Oszak discussed concerns related to neighborhood compatibility, traffic circulation, and noise impacts.
10.	Tracy McCarty, 111 Kingsley Road SE.
Ms. McCarty expressed support for Green Hedges School and discussed the school’s role in the community.
11.	Jessica Edwards-Brandt, 605 John Marshall Drive NW.
Ms. Edwards-Brandt discussed concerns regarding traffic and operational impacts on surrounding residential properties.
12.	Ann Stuntz, 2596 Chain Bridge Road.
Ms. Stuntz expressed support for the application and discussed the educational value and community role of Green Hedges School.

Board members asked several speakers questions about traffic conditions, noise impacts, buffering, and operational concerns. The applicant was given an opportunity to respond to issues raised during public testimony and to address questions related to traffic circulation, noise mitigation measures, buffering, and operational management.

Mr. Creed made a motion to close the public hearing. Mr. Gadell seconded the motion, and the motion carried.

During the public comment period, concerns were raised that the Town Hall doors had been locked, potentially preventing additional members of the public from attending and testifying. The Board discussed ensuring additional opportunities for public participation and written comments prior to taking action on the application. 

Motion: Mr. Creed moved to table the Conditional Use Permit request for Green Hedges School until the June 17, 2026, meeting and to continue accepting written public comments through Friday, May 29, 2026.

Second: Mr. Gadell

Vote: The motion carried 6–0.
EventItemTitle: 415 Windover Ave NW - Request to amend an existing Conditional Use Permit to increase number of students from 190 to 210 and staff from 42 to 50, along with associated campus, circulation, buffering, and site improvements.

Andea West
